Radha wrong: pieces not essential
Three mirrors form multiple images
Reflections of reflections
Turning gives a new pattern

questions.q: A child has a long box open at both ends and two small plane mirrors, and wants to see a game played behind a tall wall by looking over the top of the wall. Which way of fixing the mirrors makes a working periscope?
questions.a: One mirror near each opening, in a Z-shaped arrangement, slanted to face each other. Reflection from the two mirrors lets us see objects not visible directly.
o: One mirror near each opening, in a Z-shaped arrangement, slanted to face each other
Both mirrors flat against the same side wall of the box, facing the same direction
One mirror at the bottom only, facing the opening above it along the box
No mirror at all, because a long straight box lets light go round the wall

questions.q: True or False: A periscope shows objects that are not directly visible because light bends round the corners of its Z-shaped box.
questions.a: False. Light travels in straight lines. The two plane mirrors reflect it, changing its direction at each mirror, and that reflection lets us see the hidden objects.
s: Verdict: False
Correction: reflection from two mirrors, not bending round corners

questions.q: A designer says she needs fresh pattern ideas every day. (a) Which of the three devices of this chapter should she use? (b) She turns it a little each time. Why does she never see the same pattern twice?
questions.a: (a) A kaleidoscope. (b) Turning it moves the pieces and the three mirrors form multiple images (reflections of reflections), so a different pattern is seen each time.
s: Part (a): a kaleidoscope
Part (b): turning changes the multiple images formed by the three mirrors

questions.q: Meher wants to focus the image of a distant tree with her sliding pinhole camera. Describe what she does and what she will see.
questions.a: Point the pinhole towards the tree in bright sunlight, look through the open side of the smaller box with head and camera covered by a dark cloth, and move the smaller box forward or backward till the image appears on the tracing paper. The image will be upside down.
s: Pinhole faces distant object in bright sunlight
Slides the box to focus on tracing paper
Image is inverted

questions.q:
Statement 1: In a pinhole camera, rays from an object pass through a tiny hole and form an inverted image on a screen.
Statement 2: In a kaleidoscope the many patterns come from reflections of reflections in its mirrors.
Statement 3: A plane mirror image is laterally inverted but not upside down, while a pinhole camera image is upside down.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 1, 2 and 3. All three follow the chapter's account of the pinhole camera, the kaleidoscope and the comparison in the Dive Deeper.
o: 1, 2 and 3
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only

questions.q: Write three clues about a device so that a friend can identify it as a periscope, including its parts, what it does and one place where it is used.
questions.a: Clues: it has two plane mirrors in a Z-shaped box; by reflection from both mirrors it lets us see objects not directly visible; it is used in submarines, tanks or by soldiers in bunkers.
s: Clue about parts
Clue about what it does
Clue about use

questions.q: A club has a stock of loose plane mirrors. Using only the number of mirrors that the chapter's designs need, the smallest number of mirrors required to build one periscope and one kaleidoscope together is ___.
Radha says, 'A periscope and a kaleidoscope both use plane mirrors and work by reflection, but a pinhole camera uses no mirror at all.' Do you agree? Explain.
questions.a: Yes. A periscope has two plane mirrors in a Z-shaped box and a kaleidoscope has three mirror strips, so both use reflection. A pinhole camera uses a tiny hole through which rays pass to form an image on a screen, with no mirror.
s: Verdict: agrees
Periscope and kaleidoscope use plane mirrors and reflection
Pinhole camera works through a tiny hole and a screen

questions.q: A pinhole camera and a plane mirror are each placed to show a standing person. (a) What does the pinhole camera's screen show about her head and feet? (b) What does the plane mirror show about her head and feet and about her left and right hands?
questions.a: (a) The image is upside down (inverted): her feet appear at the top and her head at the bottom. (b) The mirror image is erect: her head is at the top, but her left and right are interchanged (lateral inversion).
s: Part (a): pinhole image is upside down
Part (b): mirror image erect with left and right interchanged

questions.q: Mohan removes the bangle pieces from a kaleidoscope, leaves both ends open and points it at a tree. He still sees beautiful patterns. Which reason fits the chapter?
questions.a: The three mirror strips form many images by reflections of reflections. The patterns do not depend on the bangle pieces being present.
o: The three mirror strips form many images by reflections of reflections
Light bends round the corners of the tube, so the tree is shown many times over
The tube works as a pinhole camera and forms an inverted image of the tree
The tube itself gives out light of its own, which makes the patterns appear
